All three screens are ready. Here are the two ways to separate "to read" from "finished" — same bookmarks in each, only the handling differs.

**Version A → http://maker:4001/status-a.html** — *one list with a toggle + filter buttons*
1. You'll see three example bookmarks. Each has a **"To read"** button on its right. Click the one on **"The Rise of AI Agents"** — it flips to **"✓ Finished"** and the row dims, but it stays in the list.
2. Now click the **"To read"** filter button at the top — notice only the unread ones remain visible.
3. Click **"Finished"**, then **"All"**, to see how you switch views.

**Version B → http://maker:4001/status-b.html** — *two tabs, items move between them*
1. You start on the **"To read"** tab showing two items. Click **"✓ Mark finished"** on "The Rise of AI Agents" — it disappears from this tab.
2. Click the **"Finished"** tab — it's now there, and each tab shows a count.
3. On the Finished tab, click **"↩ Move to To read"** on an item to send it back.

The difference:
- **Version A** keeps everything in **one list** and you flip a per-item switch; filter buttons narrow the view. Finished items stay visible (dimmed) unless you filter.
- **Version B** keeps your **"to read" pile clean** — finishing something moves it out of sight into a separate Finished tab.

Given your goal was to separate what you still intend to read from what you're done with, which fits better — A or B? And one thing to check: when you save a **brand-new** bookmark, should it always start as **"to read"** by default?
